title: Test Run Request
description: Canonical entry contract for an AI-driven test execution run. Produced by the Trigger Agent and consumed by the AI Crawler Agent. Every test execution in the platform begins with this object.

runId.description: Globally unique identifier for this test execution run. Assigned at creation time and used as the correlation ID across all subsequent pipeline stages.

requestId.description: Correlation identifier for the HTTP request that initiated this run. Enables tracing from the API gateway through the entire pipeline.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this run request was created. Used for ordering, auditing, and retention policies.

requestedBy.description: Identifier of the human or system that requested this run. May be a username, email, or service account name.

applicationId.description: Identifier of a previously registered application. Must be provided when the application has already been registered. Mutually exclusive with applicationName.

applicationName.description: Human-readable name for an unregistered application. Used during initial registration when applicationId has not yet been assigned. Mutually exclusive with applicationId.

baseUrl.description: The base URL of the target web application under test. Must be a valid absolute URI with an HTTP or HTTPS scheme.

environment.description: The deployment environment of the target application. Affects crawl budget, timeout defaults, and reporting severity.

crawlStrategy.description: Determines how the crawler approaches the target application. Full performs a complete crawl. Incremental re-crawls only pages flagged as changed since the last crawl. Skip bypasses crawling entirely and uses the most recent available inventory.

testLevel.description: The depth of test generation. Smoke covers only critical paths and core functionality. Regression generates comprehensive coverage across happy path, validation, and error-path scenarios.

executionMode.description: Controls how the pipeline executes — full discovery vs. reuse, and the depth of generated test coverage.

required.description: Indicates whether the target application requires authentication before it can be crawled.

loginStrategy.description: The authentication mechanism used by the target application. Form-based login with credentials. API token authentication. HTTP Basic Auth. OAuth 2.0 flow. Single sign-on via SAML or OIDC.

credentialsRef.description: Reference to the stored credentials in the credential vault. The credentials themselves are never included in the contract. Resolved at runtime by the execution service.

loginUrl.description: The URL of the login page or authentication endpoint. Required when the login strategy is form-based or OAuth.

authentication.description: Authentication configuration for accessing the target application. When required is false, all other fields are ignored.

includePages.description: URL patterns or page name filters that restrict crawling to matching pages. Patterns are matched as case-insensitive substrings against discovered URLs. An empty array means no filtering.

excludePages.description: URL patterns or page name filters that exclude matching pages from crawling. Exclusion takes precedence over inclusion. An empty array means no pages are excluded.

includeApis.description: When true, the Runtime API Discovery module analyses network traffic to discover API endpoints and their observed behaviour.

maxCrawlDepth.description: Maximum link-following depth from the starting page. Depth 1 crawls only the starting page. Higher values follow navigation links deeper into the application.

maxPages.description: Hard upper limit on the number of pages crawled. Prevents unbounded crawl time on large applications.

scope.description: Controls which parts of the target application are crawled and analysed. All scope fields are optional — an empty scope object means crawl everything discoverable.

model.description: The language model used for all AI reasoning and generation tasks in this run. Must correspond to a model available through the configured LLM provider.

temperature.description: LLM sampling temperature for this run. Lower values produce more deterministic output. The platform's default of 0.2 is appropriate for correctness-critical code generation.

reasoningLevel.description: Controls the depth of AI reasoning during test design. Low favours speed and generates straightforward scenarios. High performs multi-step reasoning for complex edge cases.

ai.description: AI model and behaviour configuration for the run. These values override the platform defaults for this run only.

timeout.description: Maximum execution time for the entire run, in seconds. If the run exceeds this limit, it is terminated and partial results are reported.

retries.description: Number of times a failed test case is re-executed before being marked as failed. Does not apply to AI agent retries, which are governed by the internal retry policy.

parallelism.description: Maximum number of Playwright test workers to run in parallel. MVP supports only sequential execution (parallelism=1). Higher values take effect in Phase 2.

browser.description: The Playwright browser engine used for crawling and test execution. MVP targets Chromium only. Firefox and WebKit support is introduced in Phase 2.

headless.description: When true, the browser runs in headless mode with no visible window. Set to false during debugging to observe browser behaviour.

execution.description: Execution runtime configuration for Playwright test runner and the overall run lifecycle.

workspace.description: Optional override for the workspace directory path. If not provided, the platform assigns a workspace based on the run ID.

artifactRetention.description: How long generated artifacts (screenshots, traces, reports, scripts) are retained after the run completes. Run-level retention means artifacts are cleaned up when the run is deleted.

output.description: Output and artifact configuration for the run. Controls where generated files are written and how long they are retained.

tags.description: Arbitrary tags for categorising runs. Used for filtering in the UI and API. Examples: 'sprint-42', 'release-candidate', 'regression-block'.

notes.description: Free-text notes describing the purpose or context of this run. Intended for human consumption.

metadata.description: User-defined metadata for organising, filtering, and documenting runs.

uuid.description: A universally unique identifier in standard 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal format.
